products.printStory: Floral in nature, but geometric and popping with color.

prints.story: Floral in nature, but geometric and popping with color.
A nod to the vibrating patterns found in Op Art of the 1960's.
One of Kati's most joyful prints. The radiating forms feel less like a pattern and more like a mood.

A sunburst repeat as seen through a kaleidescope. Kati originally painted the asterisk form in the vibrant orange, rust and yellow colorway. I added this lavender colorway for a more modern and refreshed offering.
The same asterisk form, in its original color 1970s palette.
Not a straight forward floral. Look closely and you'll find hidden hearts in the pattern.
Drawn in homage to the Matyó embroidery of Kati's birthplace. The stitchwork tradition spans generations; she translated needle to brush with the same care — dense, symmetrical, alive with color.
Delicate bunches of flowers, with an intertwining lattice of vines. Intimate, old-world and romantic.

prints.story: Delicate bunches of flowers, with an intertwining lattice of vines. Intimate, old-world and romantic.
One of the few structured prints in the archive. A grid is the antithesis of her usual organic line — but this tartan print still reads as very Kambric.

Overlapping, tumbling cherries. Mid-century European sensibility, the graphic simplicity of someone trained to look closely at ordinary, beautiful things. I recolored her original green stems to charcoal for a less literal palette.
